samples.summary: Merge-propagation block in `paste` duplicates `moveRangeTo` almost verbatim; only `clearCellsUnderMerge` was extracted
samples.evidence: paste (lines ~2314-2346) drops merges with the same loop (`mergeCoveredSrefs` -> `changedSrefs`, `store.deleteMerge`, `merges.delete`, then re-create + `rebuildMergeCoverMap`) as moveRangeTo (lines 2516-2546). The change extracted the clear-under-merge half into a helper but left the drop/re-create half copy-pasted, so the two propagate-or-reject implementations can drift. A shared `propagateMerges(dropped, created, changedSrefs, keep?)` would keep the documented "same rule cell drag-move follows" invariant in one place.

samples.summary: `cutMerges` filter for blocks only partially inside the cut source is unreachable; its comment documents behavior that cannot occur
samples.evidence: cutSourceRange is only set on the internal-paste branch, where `if (copiedMerges.some((m) => !isRangeInRange(m.range, sourceRange))) return false;` (line ~2216) already refuses any block not fully inside the source range. The later `.filter((m) => isRangeInRange(m.range, cutSourceRange!))` can therefore never drop anything, and the comment "A block only partially inside the cut source is left alone, as `moveRangeTo` refuses to split one" describes a state the code cannot reach — misleading defensive code.

samples.summary: Doc claims "merged blocks travel with an internal copy" without noting the copy buffer is per-Sheet, so a cross-sheet copy/paste silently loses merges
samples.evidence: `copyBuffer` is a private field on `Sheet` (sheet.ts:334) and merge propagation only runs in the `this.copyBuffer && text === this.copyBuffer.text` branch. Copying a merged block in one sheet and pasting into another falls through to the TSV/HTML path, where `pastedMerges` stays empty — the block is not reproduced. The new doc paragraph states the propagation rule unconditionally, so the actual limitation is undocumented.

samples.summary: A refused paste is silently a no-op at the view layer, though the package already has a host-notification channel for rejected operations
samples.evidence: spreadsheet.ts:403 and worksheet.ts:823 document a callback whose purpose is "surface a toast" when an edit is rejected by data validation. The new merge refusal path returns `false` and the views only skip `clearCopyBuffer()`; the user pressing Ctrl+V over a merged block gets no indication why nothing happened. Consistent with moveRangeTo's silent rejection, so this is a preference, but the precedent for feedback exists.

samples.summary: After a paste that re-creates a merged block, the selection is derived from the sparse grid rather than the (possibly larger) `pasteRange`
samples.evidence: `selectPastedRange(grid)` uses `rangeOf(grid)`, but the diff itself notes the copied grid is sparse because a merged block's covered cells are empty, so the computed selection can be narrower than the area actually written/merged. `pasteRange` is already computed and would be the accurate selection for the internal-paste case.

samples.summary: `rangeOf` changed from total to partial (throws on empty grid), pushing a guard onto every caller
samples.evidence: The new `if (grid.size === 0) throw new Error(...)` makes a pure coordinate helper throw; both call sites in sheet.ts (2255, 2389) must pre-check `grid.size`. Returning `undefined` (or keeping the helper total) would be a better fit for a low-level `core/coordinates` utility and would let the type system enforce the guard instead of a doc comment.
